subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep `bootstrap-extra-files` limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: This affects deterministic system-prompt context and which workspace files operators can inject automatically, so the right contract is a maintainer product/security boundary choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
options.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves guards, budgets, filtering, and docs.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and close or redirect custom-file requests to narrower first-class filename proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Keep the current restriction until a broader maintainer-approved context-loading API defines discovery, trust, and session scoping.

recommendation.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves guards, budgets, filtering, and docs.
